title: Mitigate convoying of multi-turn long-sequence requests caused by admission-window regression
creator: Priya Nair
description: Several customers across Hosted and Dedicated reported sustained latency spikes and token throughput collapse for multi-turn sessions. Triage shows a new admission-window behavior (rolled out in runtime-1.23) amplified request coalescing for long-sequence requests, causing convoying where a small number of long sequences monopolize batch slots and starve shorter/latency-sensitive flows, particularly under mixed workload patterns and Private upgrade windows.
reproduction_steps:
1) Deploy runtime-1.23 with continuous-batcher enabled on a multi-tenant node.
2) Replay mixed traffic: 5 qps of short queries (<=64 tokens) and 0.5 qps of long multi-turn sequences (>=2048 tokens) from a single tenant.
3) Observe that long sequences occupy the admission window and cause short queries to queue for several hundred milliseconds, causing tail latency spikes and degraded throughput for short flows.
investigation_notes:
- Initial heap/profile shows admission window metric (admission_slots_active) saturates for >90% when long sequences present.
- We saw an unintended regression in admission-window sizing heuristics introduced in PR #https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2145: the heuristic overshoots when sequence_length_histogram is skewed by few heavy sessions.
- Continuous prefetch handshake does not preempt inflight admission tokens, so long sequences continue to be batched even as newer short requests pile up.
- Private upgrade window observed a correlated spike because daemon restart sequenced admission tokens differently, leading to transient monopolization.
root_cause: Regression in admission-window autosizing combined with non-preemptive admission tokens. The autosizer made decisions using an arithmetic mean of recent sequence lengths, which is fragile to multi-modal workloads. Result: admission window too permissive for long sequences and lacked preemption for latency-sensitive classes.
proposed_fix_summary:
1) Replace mean-based autosizer with robust quantile estimator (p95 of recent seq lengths) to avoid being pulled by outliers.
2) Add preemptive check: mark admission tokens as preemptible for batches that contain any long sequences beyond configurable threshold, allowing ingress path to evict and prioritize latency-class requests.
3) Add tenant-weighted fairness so a single tenant cannot monopolize all admission slots.
4) Add a canary flag to runtime for gradual rollout and telemetry collection.
detailed_changes:
- runtime/scheduler/admission_autosizer.cc: implement p95 estimator and expose tunable p (default 0.95).
- runtime/scheduler/admission_token.cc: add field preemptible=true for tokens created for batches with longest_sequence > PREEMPT_SEQ_THRESHOLD.
- ingress/priority_router: honor token.preemptible and apply preemptive dequeue on new latency_request arrival.
- config: new knobs admission.p_quantile, admission.preempt_threshold_seq, admission.tenant_isolation_factor.
- metrics: admission_preempt_evictions, admission_p95_seq, admission_slot_util_p99.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for p95 estimator with synthetic skewed distributions.
- Integration tests: mixed-workload e2e where short QPS maintains tail latency under 50ms while long sequences keep throughput.
- Chaos test: restart Private nodes during upgrade windows to validate no transient monopolization.
- Load test in staging with realistic tenant mix.
- Create canary on 5% of traffic via runtime canary flag for 48 hours and monitor metrics/dashboards.
rollback_plan: Revert runtime roll containing admission autosizer change or toggle canary flag off. If partial rollout observed issues, throttle canary to 0% and revert config via feature flagging before full binary rollback.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge PR with feature-flag default off. 2) Deploy to staging; run tests and load validation. 3) Enable canary flag for 5% of Hosted traffic and Dedicated non-critical clusters for 48h. 4) If stable, ramp to 25% then 100% over 72h while monitoring metrics. 5) Coordinate Private customer upgrades with opt-in toggles and a runbook for rollback.
customer_escalation_notes:
- Customer ACME-Cloud reported 4x tail latency increase for low-latency endpoints; severity P1 raised 2026-03-09.
- Support case RED-1572: customer observed degradation during a Private upgrade window; provided temporary mitigation by disabling continuous-batcher.
- Engineering response: triage call 2026-03-10, implemented temporary ingress throttling rule to limit long-session admission to 20% of slots while fix in progress.
work_log: 2026-03-10: Triage call (Priya, Diego, Mei, Sam) - identified regression and customer impact.
2026-03-11: Hotfix applied in ingress: temporary perc_limit on long_seq tenants; short-term tail latency reduced by ~60% for ACME in staging.
2026-03-12: Root cause confirmed via trace correlation and pcap replay. Drafted design for quantile estimator and preemptive tokens.

2026-03-13: Implementation started for admission autosizer (PR #2251). Added metrics and unit tests.
Review requested from Mei and Sam.
2026-03-14: Code review feedback addressed (bounded memory for quantile buffer). Preparing canary image build.
acceptance_criteria:
- Admission p95 estimator active and passing unit tests.
- Canary on 5% of traffic shows no tail-latency regression and short-flow p99 < baseline + 10%.
- Metrics show admission_preempt_evictions > 0 during mixed workload but admission_slot_util_p99 <= target.
- Customer ACME-Cloud validates improved latency in their staging reproduction.
- No regressions on Private upgrade window tests.
